messages:
Maria: Quick update — I pushed a microbenchmark harness for kernel candidates to the perf repo. It slices by sequence length (32/128/512/2048) and runs warm/cold KV cache variants.
Sam: Nice! Does the CI run it automatically?
Maria: Yep. New job kernel-autotune-nightly runs on both a100 and h100 runners, uploads CSVs to s3://redwood-perf/kernel-candidates/YYYY-MM-DD/
Jonathon: Saw one weird regression on a100: matmul-quant8 was chosen for seq=2048 and latency jumped ~12% on cold KV.
Lee: That's expected if the selector ignores per-arch breakpoints. We need per-architecture, per-seqlen thresholds in the autotuner.
Asha: I can add a small lookup table (arch -> [seqlen_breakpoints]) and have selector pick kernel with lowest p50 cost for that bin. Fallback to previous default if deviation >3% for N runs.
ci-bot: perf job kernel-autotune-nightly completed: 38/40 kernels passed, 2 flagged (a100: matmul-quant8 @ seq2048, h100: fused-gemm @ seq512). CSVs: s3://redwood-perf/... :eyes:
Maria: PR #2345 contains the harness + CSV uploader + a tiny lookup writer. Usage:
`````
./perf/harness/run_candidates --model=gpt-2-25m --seq-lens=32,128,512,2048 --kv-modes=warm,cold --out=out.csv
`````
Sam: Can we gate merges on this job? It takes ~45m nightly but we can run a quick micro-run in PRs.
Maria: Added a short CI job kernel-candidate-quick (seqs 32/512, warm-only) that runs on PRs. Nightly is still the full sweep.
Lee: Also adding a check that flags when chosen kernel differs between archs for same seqlen and p50 delta > 5%.
Asha: I'll attach a grafana dashboard link in the PR for visual diffing.
Sam: Awesome. Please ping infra for extra h100 capacity for the next sweep :shipit:
Maria: pinging @infra on slack now. thanks :thumbsup:
